passages.context: The final paragraph was read together with the homily's title and the ANF editorial placement. It contrasts the one wrapped in swaddling clothes with the creator clothed in light, describes the manger for dumb brutes and the feeding-board for cattle, and calls Christ heavenly Bread providing spiritual sustenance. The wording is verified in Salmond's English, but author and date are not; it may be cited only as anonymous or pseudo-Gregorian transmission.
passages.notes: No manuscript, Greek text, CPG identification, or modern critical attribution was controlled. The record therefore deliberately makes no date claim beyond the 1886 English edition.

work.description: The first of four homilies transmitted and printed under Gregory Thaumaturgus's name but placed by the Ante-Nicene Fathers editors among his dubious or spurious writings. The repository records the work as anonymous and does not use it as secure evidence for Gregory or for a third-century date.
